### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 140238a47b892ef9234052e44267ec3739fa79c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ce1a746bfdf5dc51cebc686f6312f65982c966ec` — the merge of head `a6f3e6e812fc97a0bc664b54004f394713f074fe` into base `140238a47b892ef9234052e44267ec3739fa79c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ce1a746bfdf5dc51cebc686f6312f65982c966ec && git checkout ce1a746bfdf5dc51cebc686f6312f65982c966ec
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 140238a47b892ef9234052e44267ec3739fa79c2 a6f3e6e812fc97a0bc664b54004f394713f074fe && git checkout -B drift-repro 140238a47b892ef9234052e44267ec3739fa79c2 && git merge --no-ff a6f3e6e812fc97a0bc664b54004f394713f074fe

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 140238a47b892ef9234052e44267ec3739fa79c2
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a6f3e6e812fc97a0bc664b54004f394713f074fe`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23634 (body and all eight comments — the proxy ruling A `6189356908` and the dev report `6205065737` included), PR #23757 (body, the six-file list, the net diff against `main` at this head; merge base `a869ea63`), and the check-runs on this head. Read-only: `git` object reads against `origin/*` and a fetched `refs/review/pr-23757`; nothing built, run or re-run. This record is the contract verdict; it does not stand in for a check-run conclusion, and the landing still waits for every required check to read `success`.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. **The stack's `datasources` collection refuses an element whose `name` is exactly `default`** — a `superRefine` on `z.array(DatasourceSchema)` in `STACK_DEFINITION_COLLECTIONS_SHAPE`, one `custom` issue at `datasources.N.name`; the map form `datasources: { default: … }` reaches it already normalised to `name`. **RIGHT.** It is the ruling's placement (the collection, ⛔ not `DatasourceSchema`), the runtime's own comparison (`app-plugin.ts` compares `name === 'default'`), and an accepted decision rather than a new one: ADR-0062 (the #3826 second pass) records that `default` became a host-reserved name, rejected in app bundles at load and in runtime-admin create. The spelling set is exactly the runtime's: `Default`, `DEFAULT` and padded forms are refused by `DatasourceSchema.name`'s snake_case pattern, never by this rule, and that is pinned.
2. **The same refusal reaches every door that parses `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`** — `defineStack` (array and map form, `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422), the bare parse behind `os validate`, `os compile`, `os lint`'s score, the author-time rules, `scaffold-validate`, and `os migrate meta`'s post-chain `safeParse`. **RIGHT**, one contract at every door. Checked for `os migrate meta`: the chain (`applyMetaMigrationsToPackages`) runs before that `safeParse` and the config is loaded `authoredSource`, so a stack still carrying the entry gets its D3 todo listed — the changeset's sentence that `os migrate meta --from 17` lists the entry holds.
3. **Propagation into the assembled package body and the environment artifact** — `ArtifactPackageSchema` is `ManifestSchema.extend(assembledPackageBodyShape())`, which copies this collection, so `packages[].manifest.datasources` and the installed-package API arms (`options[1].manifest.datasources`, `data.options[1]…`, `data.packages.element.options[1]…`) narrow too; `EnvironmentArtifactSchema.metadata` IS `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`, so a compiled artifact and the metadata plugin's artifact rehydration (`_parseAndRegisterArtifact`) refuse it as well. **RIGHT.** A package body is loaded through `AppPlugin`, which already refuses the name, and `os compile` parses the same schema, so no artifact carrying the entry can be produced. The PR body names these only as the four ledger sites and as "publish"; they are accept-set narrowings in their own right and are judged here.
4. **The host's own `default` row keeps parsing** — `DatasourceSchema` is untouched; `DefaultDatasourcePlugin.record()` and its `registerInMemory('datasource', 'default', …)` go through the per-document schema, never through a stack collection; no export path on `origin/main` builds a stack-shaped document with `datasources` from the metadata manager. **RIGHT**, and pinned by the CONTROL.
5. **No config that boots today is newly refused** — checked on `origin/main`: no `name: 'default'` datasource in `examples/`, `packages/create-objectstack`, `skills/` or `content/docs` (`drivers.mdx`'s map-form example declares `analytics` and `cache`; `metadata-service.mdx:277` shows the host's own row via `registerInMemory`, not a stack). The one in-repo instance, `default-datasource-plugin.test.ts:332`, hands a raw bundle to `AppPlugin` and stays green. The fallback clause of ruling `6189356908` is not triggered. **RIGHT.**
6. **Published JSON Schema bytes are unchanged; the gap is recorded** — `z.toJSONSchema()` projects no `custom` check, so the four sites join `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` (759 → 763). **RIGHT** under that ledger's own design: hand-edited, no `gen:` script, a new gap has to be a reviewed line in a diff, and the build refuses until the line moves. None of the five closed projection arms (`banned-key-pattern`, `banned-keys`, `dependent-required`, `non-blank-string`, `required-one-of`) states "an element's `name` is not X"; adding one is, per the ledger, a public-contract decision and is correctly not made here.
7. **Public API surface: unchanged** — `HOST_RESERVED_DATASOURCE_NAME` and the refiner are module-private; no export added, removed or renamed; `check:generated` 14/14 up to date per the report and the `Type Check · source gates` run is green. **RIGHT.**
8. **`z.array(DatasourceSchema)` kept on one line** for `check:stack-collection-maps`'s census. **RIGHT**, a spelling constraint of the census, no semantic change.
9. **Untouched as the ruling and claim require**: `DatasourceSchema`, `serve.ts` (PR #23631's remedy line), `skills/**`, `content/docs/releases/`. **RIGHT.** File list: six files, none on a governed surface; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green; head repo = base repo; 352 / 2 changed lines, under the 3,000 line human-merge threshold.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23634-stack-datasource-default-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, summary `feat(spec)!: …`, a `**BREAKING**` paragraph, the direction arm written as `no (narrowing)` on its declaration line, and the adr-0087 HTML-comment marker `registered stack-datasource-host-reserved-name-refused`, matching the D3 entry id. **RIGHT.** The diff publishes one accept-set narrowing from one released package; `packages/cli` gains only a test. Under `.changeset/pre.json` (pre mode) and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s launch-window guard a breaking change ships as `minor`, with breaking-ness carried by the `!`, the banner and the `narrowing` arm that `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` reads through `readClause2Line`. `Check Changeset` green. The FROM → TO table and the one-line fix are present, as a breaking changeset must carry.
- The declaration line: the PR body reads `no` (the claim-time ceiling in `6203348600`); the changeset reads `no (narrowing)`. **RIGHT, not a mismatch**: the arm is read from the changeset by the ADR-0087 gate, and the PR body's bare `no` is the same declaration without the arm that gate does not read there. A narrowing is not a widening, so `no` with the `narrowing` arm is the one legal spelling (`(narrowing)` is BREAKING; `no (widening)` would be malformed).
- No `skip-changeset`; none would be right.
- D3 entry `18.stack-datasource-host-reserved-name-refused.ts`: `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria` filled; no `conversionIds` (nothing is mechanically convertible, which the entry says); `relevantWhen` omitted — the surface also lives under `packages[].manifest.datasources`, so a top-level-keys question would misreport a package body, and always-listed is the conservative reading of the type's own rule. **RIGHT.**

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (report `6205065737`):
- `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` outside the claimed surface — **answered**: a gate-required artifact under the claim's "generated outputs, if the gates ask" clause, hand-edited by that ledger's design; judged in ① item 6.
- `cca45a7e` (wip) carries no `Claude-Session` / `Co-authored-by` pair, and the merge commit `a6f3e6e8` likewise — **answered**: the queue lands by squash, so neither message reaches `main`; the pre-push hook refuses a model identifier, not an absent pair; pushed history stays unrewritten per the rule. Not blocking.
- The CLI unit tier needed a cli build, and dists other than spec and cli were not rebuilt after the `origin/main` merge — **answered**: local-only; CI builds fresh (`Build Core` and `TypeScript Type Check` green on this head).

Dev `open_questions`:
- **The skills line** `skills/objectstack-data/rules/datasources.md:4-6` ("Most apps need only the `default` datasource; declare more …") — **escalated to the skills lane**, as ruling `6189356908` itself directs (⛔ no `skills/**` edit rides this PR; `skills/**` is a Tier H surface). Recommendation A, the rewording in the PR's acceptance notes. Owning seat: file or route the one-line card.
- **One sentence, three sites** (spec, `app-plugin.ts`, `datasource-admin-service.ts`) — **escalated**: exporting the reserved name and its sentence from spec is an api-surface addition plus a `packages/runtime` edit, outside this claim; option A as its own follow-up card, B (synonymous, each door's own) for this PR. Not blocking.

Dev out-of-scope finding (the published JSON Schema stays wider than the parse at these four sites) — **answered**: recorded in the ledger (① item 6); closing it is a projection-arm decision for the spec lane, not this card.

Reviewer's own flags:
- `packages/cli/test/stack-datasource-default-validate-door.test.ts` is integration-tier (two `tsx` spawns, 180 s timeouts) and declares no `// test-budget:` header; its wall is in none of the inputs. `check-test-suite-ceilings` is report-only; if the refresh window reads the file above 10 s it is the lane's card (ruling record 6181973363), never a gate. Recorded, not blocking.
- Check-runs on this head, read at 2026-10-16T00:43Z: `Lint & Repo Gates` success, `TypeScript Type Check` success, `Build Core` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success; `Test Core`: shards 1, 2, 5, 6 success (every completed shard), shards 3, 4 still in progress at this read, so the required `Test Core` context has not reported; this head is not yet green on that context, the owning seat re-reads it before arming anything, and a PASS here is the contract verdict only. Advisory: `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check PR Size` and the claim / single-writer / part-of guards all success; the full-battery jobs are skipped on a PR run by design.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · objectstack `domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549) · session `session_01LFqdRsuM5nkqoJdHd5ztVk` · 2026-10-16T00:46Z

This is the seat review of record for #23634 (triage's proxy ruling A `6189356908`, claim `6203348600`), on head `a6f3e6e812fc97a0bc664b54004f394713f074fe`.

1. **Form.**
   - Draft to `main`. The first line is `Fixes #23634`; the second is `Clause-②: no`, as the claim set it. The changeset carries `no (narrowing)`, which the ADR-0087 gate reads (contract review ②).
   - 6 files, +352/−2. One BREAKING changeset: `@objectstack/spec` minor (pre mode), disposition `registered stack-datasource-host-reserved-name-refused`, which matches the D3 entry's id.
2. **What it does.**
   - A `superRefine` on the stack's `datasources` collection refuses an entry named exactly `default`. The issue is located at `datasources.N.name` and covers the array form and the map form.
   - The text carries the runtime's sentence and the ruling's remedy: set `OS_DATABASE_URL`, or declare the datasource under another name and route objects to it.
   - The refusal sits on the collection, ⛔ not on `DatasourceSchema`. The host's own `default` row still parses; that is a pinned CONTROL.
   - The comparison is the runtime's `name === 'default'`. Every other spelling already fails `DatasourceSchema.name`'s pattern (pinned).
   - Untouched, as the ruling requires: `DatasourceSchema`, `serve.ts` and `skills/**`.
3. **The fallback clause holds.** The dev re-measured the R4 shape: under `OS_DATABASE_URL` and under `--dev`, it exits 1 with `AppPlugin`'s refusal. This agrees with the card's M1–M4. In-repo producers: none. No config that boots today is newly refused.
4. **Gates.**
   - CI on this head at 00:45Z: 40 check-runs. Every completed run is `success` or a fast-set `skip`. `Test Core` 3/6 and 4/6 are still `in_progress`; auto-merge waits on them.
   - Dev local: 90 derived families, 90 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, on the merge head.
   - Ablation: the refusal made a no-op, with a dist leg proven by `ablation-dist-preflight`. The 4 refusal pins went red, the 3 controls stayed green, and the CLI door went 1 red / 1 green. Restored. The dev reports two earlier no-op legs and does not count them.
5. **Contract review:** PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, comment `6205386930`, on this head. No judgment was marked WRONG.
6. **Open questions** (report `6205065737`).
   - **Q1, the skills line: answered A, through the skills lane.** The ruling's own clause sends this there. The dev measured `skills/objectstack-data/rules/datasources.md:4-6` ("declare more"), and it invites the refused shape. Filed as #23768 (`domain:skills`, `priority:p2`, Tier H, `Blocked-by: #23757`), with the dev's wording. ⛔ No `skills/**` edit rides this PR.
   - **Q2, one sentence at three sites: answered B, keep three synonymous sentences; no card.**
     - Startup focus: exporting the name and the sentence from `@objectstack/spec` adds a public api-surface entry with no consumer pulling for it.
     - AI-proofing: the authoring refusal now fires first, at `os validate`. The runtime and admin-door sentences are each pinned by their own door's tests, so drift between them misleads no author.
     - Long-term fit: `default` is a fixed host contract (#3826), not a name expected to move.
     - The contract review leaned to A as a follow-up. The seat records the disagreement here; a later case where the three actually drift would reopen it.
7. **Accepted deviations.**
   - `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json` (+4 sites, 759 → 763) is outside the named surface. The build requires it, and it is hand-maintained by the ledger's design. No projection arm fits ("an element's `name` is not X"); adding one is a public-contract decision for the spec lane.
   - The wip commit `cca45a7e` lacks the trailer pair. The PR squashes, so it never reaches `main`.
   - The two CLI unit files that needed a local `cli` build passed after it. CI builds fresh.
   - The reviewer's flag that the new CLI integration test has no `// test-budget:` header is not a gate. It goes to the lane card if the suite-ceiling census reads it over budget.
8. **Landing terms.** Ready, then auto-merge. `Fixes #23634` closes the card on merge. No generated artifact moved except the hand-kept ledger, so this PR is outside the relay order of #23708 and #23710.
